deities: Goddess Kali as Dakshina Kali, worshipped as Karunamoyee ('the compassionate mother')

history.summary: Famous Lake Kalibari of Kolkata; identity confirmed. Official name: Sree Sree 108 Karunamoyee Kalimata Mandir, located at 1 Southern Avenue, beside Rabindra Sarobar (Dhakuria Lake) — hence 'Lake Kalibari'. Founded in 1949 by Haripada Chakraborty, a devotee of Maa Kali and tantra sadhak who, after receiving swapnadesh (dream-command) from the goddess, established her idol in a 'Panchamundi ashana' (seat of five skulls), initially in a thatched patar kutir hut, later rebuilt as a temple. Managed by the Sree Sri Karunamoyee Kalimata Trust (official site lakekalibari.org). Wikipedia notes reconstruction has been underway since 2002 but remains incomplete for lack of funds (verify current status).

name: Lake Kalibari
town_description: Kolkata, the capital of West Bengal, is a major metropolis on the Hooghly river — India's cultural capital, famous for its intense Kali worship centered on Kalighat and Dakshineswar; the Southern Avenue/Rabindra Sarobar area of South Kolkata is the temple's leafy neighbourhood.

travel.airport: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU), roughly 25 km away.
travel.railway: Ballygunge Junction, under 2 km away; Kalighat metro is nearby.
travel.road: 1 Southern Avenue, Lake Terrace, Ballygunge, South Kolkata, beside Rabindra Sarobar; walkable from Southern Avenue crossings.

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Kali Puja (Kartik Amavasya) and Kaushiki Amavasya are the major days.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported 6 AM-9:30 PM daily on the temple's site; Justdial says 8 AM-10 PM (conflicting — verify).
